harvard-on-edge.name: Harvard Making Caring Common: On Edge (2024), drivers of young adults' mental health challenges

lacked-meaning.name: Lacked meaning or purpose in the previous month
lacked-meaning.passage: Nearly 3 in 5 young adults (58%) reported that they lacked “meaning or purpose” in their lives in the previous month.

not-knowing-what-to-do.name: Not knowing what to do with my life
not-knowing-what-to-do.passage: Half of young adults reported that their mental health was negatively influenced by “not knowing what to do with my life.”

not-mattering.name: A sense of not mattering to others
not-mattering.passage: Forty-four percent (44%) of young adults reported a sense of not mattering to others and 34% reported loneliness.

ons-wellbeing.name: ONS Public opinions and social trends, Great Britain (February 2026): personal well-being

low-worthwhile.name: Low levels of feeling that the things they do in life are worthwhile
low-worthwhile.passage: Almost 1 in 10 adults (9%) reported low levels of feeling that the things they do in life are worthwhile; this was more common among adults aged 16 to 29 years (14%) and 30 to 49 years (11%).

nces-piaac-2023.name: NCES: U.S. PIAAC 2023 national results (adult skills)

low-literacy.name: Literacy at Level 1 or below
low-literacy.passage: Between 2017 and 2023, there were increases in the percentages of adults performing at the lowest proficiency level (Level 1 or below) in both literacy and numeracy: in literacy this percentage increased from 19 to 28 percent and in numeracy from 29 to 34 percent.

low-numeracy.name: Numeracy at Level 1 or below
low-numeracy.passage: Between 2017 and 2023, there were increases in the percentages of adults performing at the lowest proficiency level (Level 1 or below) in both literacy and numeracy: in literacy this percentage increased from 19 to 28 percent and in numeracy from 29 to 34 percent.

low-problem-solving.name: Adaptive problem solving at the lowest level
low-problem-solving.passage: The percentage of U.S. adults performing at the lowest level in adaptive problem solving in 2023 was 32 percent.

air-digital-literacy.name: NCES/AIR: A Description of U.S. Adults Who Are Not Digitally Literate

not-digitally-literate.name: Adults who are not digitally literate
not-digitally-literate.passage: About 16 percent of U.S. adults are not digitally literate, compared to 23 percent of adults internationally.

census-language.name: U.S. Census Bureau: language spoken at home and ability to speak English, ACS 2018-2022

english-less-than-very-well.name: Speaks English less than "very well"
english-less-than-very-well.passage: Among the population age 5 and older that spoke a language other than English at home, 61.0% of Spanish speakers, 48.2% of Chinese speakers (which includes all dialects), and 69.8% of Tagalog (including Filipino) speakers spoke English “very well.”

no-high-school-diploma.name: Less than a high school diploma or equivalent
no-high-school-diploma.passage: In 2022, the highest level of education of the population age 25 and older in the United States ranged from less than high school to advanced degrees beyond a bachelor’s degree. 9% had less than a high school diploma or equivalent.

schedules.name: Training schedules
schedules.passage: Of those who wanted to participate and could not (10.2%) or those who participated but wanted to participate more (15.7%), 25.3% listed training schedules as the main barrier to their participation, while 16.0% cited family reasons, and 15.2% highlighted costs

ferrari-procrastination.name: Ferrari: prevalence of chronic procrastination (Psychology Today summary of his studies)

chronic-procrastination.name: Chronic procrastinators
chronic-procrastination.passage: In a 1991 published study (Ferrari, 1991a) I found that 20 percent of adult women and men self-identify as “chronic procrastinators,” meaning they purposively delay tasks at home, school, work, in relationships, appointments.

adult-literacy.passage: The average rate of literacy needs across the OECD is 26%

adult-numeracy.name: Adult numeracy skills (Survey of Adult Skills 2023)
adult-numeracy.passage: The average rate of numeracy needs across the OECD is 25%.

youth-neet.passage: The share of youth not in employment, education or training has risen markedly in one fifth of OECD countries (Estonia, Chile, Slovenia, Lithuania, Poland, US).

sdg-targets.name: UN SDG targets bearing on learning, skills and direction

4.3.name: 4.3 Equal access to affordable technical, vocational and tertiary education
4.3.passage: 4.3 By 2030, ensure equal access for all women and men to affordable and quality technical, vocational and tertiary education, including university

4.4.name: 4.4 Relevant skills for employment, decent jobs and entrepreneurship
4.4.passage: 4.4 By 2030, substantially increase the number of youth and adults who have relevant skills, including technical and vocational skills, for employment, decent jobs and entrepreneurship

4.6.name: 4.6 Literacy and numeracy for youth and adults
4.6.passage: 4.6 By 2030, ensure that all youth and a substantial proportion of adults, both men and women, achieve literacy and numeracy

8.6.name: 8.6 Reduce youth not in employment, education or training
8.6.passage: 8.6 By 2020, substantially reduce the proportion of youth not in employment, education or training
